_doc: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B/13B MoE) benchmark config — p5.48xlarge (8×H100). DSPARK-ONLY REGIME (nospec was completed on v0.24.0 in the 2026-07-09 run; those 106 cells stay in S3, this sweep only fills in dspark). EP swept as on/off per sharding. CP omitted (no supported sparse-MLA CP path on sm_90). FP4 experts run via dequant on Hopper (native on Blackwell); headline numbers are a lower bound vs B200/B300.

regime.spec: Speculative decoding via DSpark (k=7, greedy) on vLLM main-branch nightly-95ed0feaa (2026-07-10), REQUIRED because method='dspark' landed post-v0.24.0. The 2026-07-09 nospec cells here were measured on v0.24.0 — DIFFERENT engine. Report spec-vs-nospec as absolute numbers + acceptance (per-cell image is in each run_manifest.json), not a clean speedup. Also: this bench uses `--dataset random` with `random_range_ratio=0`, which is a floor case for spec decode — DSpark's paper reports acceptance-length τ≈3.5-6 on natural-language benchmarks, this bench observed τ≈1.3 (random tokens give the predictive drafter little to draft). Real production speedup will be substantially higher than what shows here.

instance.p5: DSV4-Flash's FP4 expert kernels run via dequant on Hopper (native FP4 math is Blackwell / sm_100 only), so all headline throughput here is a LOWER BOUND on what B200/B300 would deliver at the same op-point.

_image_note: Pinned main-branch nightly (2026-07-10). REQUIRED for the dspark regime: method='dspark' landed via PR #46995 (2026-07-01) + #47093 (2026-07-02), which is AFTER v0.24.0's release (2026-06-29) — on v0.24.0 SpeculativeConfig rejects it at engine-config validation ('container exited before becoming healthy'). Verified at this SHA: config/speculative.py has Literal['dspark'] + dspark model files present. CROSS-ENGINE CAVEAT: the 106 nospec cells from the 2026-07-09 run were measured on v0.24.0; dspark cells run on this nightly. Per-cell provenance is in each run_manifest.json ('image' field). Report spec-vs-nospec as absolute numbers + acceptance, not a clean speedup (same caveat pattern as the Gemma study's 0.20.0/0.22.1 split).

models._safetensors_prefetch_note: REQUIRED on ext4 (this DLAMI's /scratch): the default lazy-mmap load strategy deadlocked all 8 workers in random-read safe_open for 28+ min with 0% GPU util. Prefetch flag (per vLLM issue #40988) loads shards into page cache first, then workers read sequentially — took 40s per rank. Not usually needed on NFS (vLLM auto-detects and prefetches there); ext4 auto-detect said 'local, use lazy', and lazy hung.
models._rope_scaling_note: Intentionally NOT set: the HF checkpoint's own config.json bakes the identical YaRN rope_scaling (verified 2026-07-10). vLLM main-branch nightly (post-6d29d80) removed the `--rope-scaling` CLI arg, so passing it explicitly is (a) redundant and (b) fatal on the nightly. Restore this ONLY if a future model doesn't bake rope_scaling into its own config.

regimes.name: dspark
regimes._doc: DSpark speculative decoding k=7 greedy. INTENTIONAL k=7 (NOT the mistake SKILL.md line 129 warns against): 7 is DSpark's TRAINING block size (the '_block7' checkpoint), and this run is deliberately the training-block-size baseline per SKILL.md option 3 ('label the sweep as training-block-size baseline, not deployment-tuned'). It is NOT trying to reproduce the paper's headline speedup — that needs the paper's deployment γ=5, which would be a SEPARATE deployment-tuned pass. Do NOT silently change this to 5; that would change what the run measures. Uses the -DSpark checkpoint (hf_id_by_regime). This is the ONLY regime in this run — nospec was completed on v0.24.0 in the 2026-07-09 run; those 106 cells live in S3 under dsv4_flash__nospec/ and dsv4_flash__nospec_ep/ and are combined with these dspark results at deliverables time (cross-engine footnote).

_shardings: tp1_dp8 excluded (145GB won't fit 80GB/GPU even with EP). tp2_dp4 without EP likely OOMs (36GB/GPU weight + 256 unsharded experts); the per-cell OOM guard will skip it. tp2_dp4 ep:true listed because EP distributes experts across 8 ranks.
_workload: random_range_ratio 0.0 (exact lengths) for the Gemma-comparable grid — same rationale as the Gemma study. DSV4's YaRN handles the context extension; exact lengths keep prompt-length controlled across cells.
_server: block_size=256 per the DSpark recipe (matches V4's CSA block stride). --language-model-only disables multimodal (text-only bench, same as Gemma). kv_cache_dtype fp8 fixed across all regimes per user spec. tokenizer/tool/reasoning parser flags + cudagraph compilation config from the vLLM DSV4 recipe — cudagraph size 128 matches our conc ceiling; watch for a throughput cliff at conc=128 vs conc=64 (indicates conc=128 fell out of the captured graph). NOTE: --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch is emitted by the harness (see models[0].safetensors_prefetch), NOT here — it needs to be per-model, not universal.
_docker_env: HF_TOKEN auto-forwarded by sweep_bench.py from the host env. Add VLLM_PLUGINS or CUDA env vars here if needed.
_save_detailed: Capture per-request ITLs for 10%-trimmed-mean TPOT and latency distribution analysis.
